new_statements.rule_in_words: Kendem is described as a two-tone language (underlying H and L, with derived surface contours), like Kenyang and Denya; the source makes no statement about word stress or accent for Kendem.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone on words in citation form (minimal pairs given); no prosodic-word or phrase-level stress discussion.
new_statements.identity_note: Ojong 2005 treats 'Kendem' as one of three Nyang languages (with Kenyang and Denya) and notes it has no reference dialect; Anderson & Krüger 2004 survey the villages Kendem, Kekpoti and Bokwa (Bokwa-Kendem = kend1252). No dialect mismatch.

sources.note: Sec. 2.3 'Kendem Phonology' (pp. 21-23) gives 17 consonants, 6 vowels, syllable types and Sec. 2.3.4 'Tones' (p. 23): two underlying tones, High and Low, with several surface realizations. Nothing at all on stress or accent for Kendem; the only occurrence of 'stress' in the thesis (p. 13, Sec. 1.8) describes Tyhurst's 1984 report on KENYANG phonology as containing 'an analysis of suprasegmental features of stress, length, and tone'.
